Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.

## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)

- OBJECT-INDEX, batch B0056, scope METHODOLOGICAL: "A self-audit comparing the '00/01' corpus-baseline-plus-DEL-compatibility documents against the separately-developed Dretske/K_t mathematical research line, concluding they are NOT the same but have large overlap, organized into three layers: Layer 1 (corpus-established results: Sigma!=K_i, K_t!=possible-world model, Conflict allowed, A not deductively closed, governance!=epistemic-update, information!=meaning!=knowledge); Layer 2 (Dretske-derived additions not in 00/01: the World->Observation->Channel->Signal->Information->Probability->Determination->K_t acquisition chain, and channel reliability/calibration); Layer 3 (the newer atomic-claim mathematical model k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,C_i,p_i,q_i), the X*!=K_t!=I_t(P,C) three-way split, and the vector gap G_t, none of which appear in 00/01). Reports the '00' document's own claim that there are 'two rival definitions of K_t and zero shared symbols' in the corpus baseline, and warns against retrospectively pretending the newer atomic-claim model was already the corpus's definition. Prescribes an explicit four-stage provenance discipline for K_t claims: [CORPUS] (K_t has competing definitions, unresolved formalization) -> [EXT] (Dretske/probability/information-theory/DEL supply external structures) -> [INF] (those theories constrain, but do not determine, a plausible K_t model) -> [PROP] (the proposed k_i tuple and K_t(O)={k_i} construction), concluding the correct summary is 'the corpus has not yet ratified a unique formal definition of K_t; external-theory analysis has ruled out or constrained several candidate interpretations; current research has produced a more explicit [PROP] candidate' rather than 'we have now defined K_t.'"
